paper_id: Hierarchical Federated Learning through LAN-WAN Orchestration
title: Hierarchical Federated Learning through LAN-WAN Orchestration
motivation: WAN-driven FL incurs high monetary cost (80% of cost is network traffic) and slow convergence (Google reports 3000 rounds, 5 days for RNN)
problem_framing: Traditional FL requires 500-10,000 cloud rounds across constrained WAN; need hierarchical aggregation: intra-LAN (frequent) + inter-LAN (infrequent)
key_insight: LAN abundant bandwidth (tens of Mbps) can be exploited for frequent local aggregation, reducing reliance on expensive constrained WAN
method_signature: LanFL: two-level aggregation hierarchy with P2P intra-LAN topology and dynamic device selection for heterogeneous LAN
evaluation_criteria: Model accuracy, convergence speed (clock time), WAN traffic reduction, monetary cost savings
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: LanFL relies on manual parameter tuning through extensive experiments; current design only works for LAN domains with ≥10 devices, introducing selection bias
evidence_for_taste: such a cost can be amplified
thinking_moves: 把通信瓶颈重新定位到局域网层级而非广域网
从成本结构(网络费用占比)推导优化方向
层级化设计: 局部聚合+全局聚合的分治策略
通过实验发现AP数量影响拓扑选择(PS vs Ring)
异构性导致同步等待问题 → 动态设备选择平衡训练节奏
